name: PHQ-9
shortDescription: 9-item validated depression severity scale widely used to monitor mood changes over time.
timeframe: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
citation: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JB. J Gen Intern Med. 2001;16(9):606-613.

questions.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed — or the opposite, being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way
If you checked off any problems, how difficult have these problems made it for you to do your work, take care of things at home, or get along with other people?

scoring.formulaDescription: Sum of items Q1–Q9 scored 0–3 each (range 0–27); Q10 records functional impairment for clinical context without adding to the score. Cutoffs at 5, 10, 15, and 20 mark mild, moderate, moderately severe, and severe depression.

safetyFlags.message: You indicated thoughts of self-harm or being better off dead. Please consider reaching out for support — in the US & Canada call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), contact your local emergency or crisis helpline, or reach out to a trusted person or healthcare professional.
